sentence: This project tries to find therapeutic agents that could prevent or stabilize aortic aneurysm in patients with Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, using preclinical patient models.
This project builds a platform to record brain activity and behavior in a highly social songbird living in a complex social setting.
This project studies how DNA damage in cancer cells activates nucleic acid sensing pathways that change immune responses against tumors.
This project builds a technique to find breast cancers that screening digital breast tomosynthesis images miss in women with dense breast tissue.
This project builds a humanized mouse model that uses tumor tissue and immune cells from one patient to study immunotherapies for glioblastoma.
This project combines a targeted nanoparticle rinse with an intraoral camera to better detect early dental caries and monitor treatment.
This project tests which features of pre-exposure prophylaxis products people in the Philippines prefer, including the use of hormone therapy alongside it.
This project studies the molecular steps by which herpesviruses move viral capsids out of the nucleus and into the cytoplasm.
This project supports four resource cores that give vision researchers imaging, gene expression, protein measurement and statistical tools to study blinding diseases.
This project studies how lipid-laden macrophages and Staphylococcus aureus interact to form abscesses in the bone marrow during osteomyelitis.
This project tests a natural killer cell engager in a clinical trial for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
This project studies how budding yeast controls its cell shape, using gene editing, live-cell imaging and biochemistry.
This project builds a generative framework that makes large public cranial image datasets to study how craniosynostosis affects cranial development in children.
This project builds a platform using cloud computing and quantum technologies to find sweat-based biomarkers for noninvasive tracking of Parkinson's disease.
This project tests whether contact with pets protects patients from gut microbiome disruption and infection with Clostridioides difficile after antimicrobial therapy.
This project studies how the gut microbiome and other host factors set urine oxalate levels, using mouse models and patient studies.
This project tries to find out what role fatty acids play in the brain after neonatal brain injury from extremely preterm birth.
This project tests whether mRNA and vector-based vaccines carrying an antigen can protect against coccidioidomycosis and also work as immunotherapy.
This project tries to find out how chromatin regulation helps bladder cancer evade the immune system, including how it represses antigen presentation.
This project uses imaging, single cell RNA sequencing and cancer vaccine design to show how lymphatics can help personalize immune responses against cancer.
